title: Every morphism from a single object factors through the bottom-homology inclusion
statement: Let C be an abelian category with a derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let n be any integer, and let M be an object of D+(C) with no homology in degrees below n. Define j_n(M):H^n(M)[-n] \to M as the inverse canonical double-truncation isomorphism, followed by the inverse lower projection of the upper truncation, followed by its upper inclusion. For every Y in C and f:Y[-n] \to M, one has f=single_n(c_n(Y)^{-1} followed by H^n(f)) followed by j_n(M), where c_n is the specified single/homology isomorphism.

source.place: 05TC (2), canonical double truncation; 05TD (3), actual derived unit. Canonical-map calculation written by R2 from the parent node and the named library comparisons.

proof.text: Naturality of the upper inclusion factors f through the upper truncation of M, using the invertible upper inclusion on Y[-n]. The lower projection of that upper truncation is invertible since M has no homology below n.

Apply single-source homology extensionality to the map into the double truncation followed by its single-object isomorphism. Its homology formula and naturality of the single/homology comparison give the specified coefficient. Compose with the inverse double identification, inverse lower projection and upper inclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem single_map_bottomHomologyInclusion (n : ℤ) (M : Plus C) [M.IsGE n]
    (Y : C) (f : (singleFunctor C n).obj Y ⟶ M) :
    f = (singleFunctor C n).map
        ((singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso n).inv.app Y ≫
          (homologyFunctor C n).map f) ≫ bottomHomologyInclusion n M
